links.outcome: Validity of citations generated by GPT-4.0 against identifiable database references
links.effect: GPT-4.0 cited 86 references (2.46 per answer), only 50% deemed valid, and 77.1% of responses contained at least one inappropriate citation.
links.quote: Moreover, GPT-4.0 cited 86 references (2.46 citations per answer), of which only 50 % were deemed valid, and 77.1 % of responses contained at least one inappropriate citation.

links.outcome: Consistency with current guidelines, incorporation of recent advances, and missed red-flag symptoms in neurosurgical answers
links.effect: Responses consistent with guidelines 92.8% and accounted for recent advances 78.6% of the time; red flag symptoms missed 7.1% of the time.
links.quote: GPT-4.0 responses were consistent with current medical guidelines and accounted for recent advances in the field 92.8 % and 78.6 % of the time respectively.

links.outcome: Missed red flag symptoms in GPT-4.0 neurosurgical responses
links.effect: "Red flag" symptoms were missed 7.1% of the time; depth of clinical responses varied (3.7 ± 0.6).
links.quote: The depth of clinical responses varied (3.7 ± 0.6), and "red flag" symptoms were missed 7.1 % of the time.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation by expert clinicians of GPT-4's performance, safety, and citation accuracy on simulated clinical neurosurgery questions, without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
